title: Red-QAOA: Efficient Variational Optimization through Circuit Reduction
problem: QAOA's parameter optimization is severely degraded by noise, and larger problems requiring more qubits become increasingly noise-sensitive, limiting practical applicability to larger combinatorial optimization instances.
motivation: Mitigating noise in quantum approximate optimization is critical for scaling QAOA to practical combinatorial optimization problems.
method: Red-QAOA employs simulated annealing-based graph reduction to concentrate the energy landscape while reducing problem size. By decreasing the graph size, the algorithm requires fewer qubits while maintaining optimization quality. This concentrates the parameter search space to achieve robustness against noise perturbations.
key_novelty: Using energy landscape concentration via simulated annealing-based graph reduction to improve noise robustness in QAOA parameter optimization.
contributions: Identifies noise sensitivity as a critical bottleneck in QAOA scalability
Proposes Red-QAOA algorithm combining graph reduction with simulated annealing guidance
Demonstrates energy landscape concentration for improved parameter robustness
Reduces qubit requirements while maintaining solution quality
